**Perioperative Fasting (2-4-6-8 Rule)** ★★ — Clear liquids ==2 h==, breast milk ==4 h==, formula/milk/light meal ==6 h==, fatty/meat meal ==8 h==; ==never== delay emergency surgery for fasting.

## Elective fasting intervals ★★

| Intake category | Minimum fast | Examples / boundary |
|---|---|---|
| **Clear liquids** ★★ | ==2 hours== | Water, black coffee/tea ==without milk==, pulp-free clear juice |
| **Breast milk** ★ | ==4 hours== | Human breast milk |
| **Infant formula / non-human milk** | ==6 hours== | Cow milk, infant formula |
| **Light meal** ★ | ==6 hours== | Toast + clear liquid |
| **Fried, fatty, or meat meal** ★ | ==8 hours== | Heavy / high-fat solid meal |

## High-risk full stomach & practice rules

- **Hydration:** encourage clear liquids ==up to 2 hours before induction== (prevents dehydration and perioperative hypoglycaemia).
- **Delayed gastric emptying** ★★: diabetes with gastroparesis, pregnancy, bowel obstruction, severe obesity, or recent opioids ==may still retain gastric contents even after 8 hours== → consider gastric POCUS before induction.

## ⚠ Never

- ==Do not== keep healthy elective patients nil by mouth from midnight unnecessarily.
- ==Never delay emergency surgery== solely to satisfy elective fasting intervals — treat as full stomach and use rapid-sequence induction ==when indicated== ★★.

## Cards

- Minimum elective fasting intervals (2-4-6-8 rule) → Clear liquids 2 h (no milk), breast milk 4 h, infant formula/non-human milk/light meal 6 h, fried/fatty/meat meal 8 h
- Does coffee with milk count as a clear liquid for the 2-hour rule? → No; clear liquids require coffee or tea without milk (non-human milk requires 6 hours)
- Should healthy elective patients be kept nil by mouth from midnight? → No; do not fast from midnight unnecessarily — encourage clear liquids up to 2 hours before induction
- How do elective fasting intervals apply to emergency surgery? → Never delay emergency surgery solely to satisfy elective fasting intervals; treat as full stomach and use RSI when indicated
- Which conditions may cause retained gastric contents even after 8 hours of fasting? → Diabetes with gastroparesis, pregnancy, bowel obstruction, severe obesity, or recent opioid use (consider gastric POCUS)
